title: He was already chosen…
paragraphs:
He was already chosen…
but still treated like he didn’t matter.
Because some of you are living in that exact tension right now.
You know there’s something on your life.

But instead of a crown…
you were given a harp in a hostile room.
And here’s the question that won’t leave you alone:
“Why am I serving people who don’t even see me?”

Why are you pouring out
in places that drain you?

Why are you faithful
in rooms that feel spiritually heavy?

Why are you healing others
while quietly breaking inside?
Because David wasn’t just playing music.
He was stepping into someone else’s torment.
Every time he touched those strings… he felt the weight of Saul’s darkness.

And David—young, anointed, chosen—sat there…
and played anyway.
Some of you are angry at your “harp season.”
It’s actually where God is forming you the most?

David had oil on his head…
but still had to serve a broken man.

David carried a promise…
but still had to endure pressure.

David knew his future…
but still showed up in obedience.

“Whenever the spirit from God came on Saul, David would take up his lyre and play. Then relief would come to Saul… and the evil spirit would leave him.”
— 1 Samuel 16:23
David’s worship didn’t just sound good.
Some scholars interpret this passage as God allowing a distressing spirit as judgment on Saul’s rebellion.
Others see it as a spiritual oppression permitted by God’s sovereignty.

You may be in a room not because of your failure…
but because of someone else’s brokenness.
And God trusted you to bring His presence there.

You start serving…
and slowly your heart begins to whisper:
Pride starts disguising itself as frustration.
This is where many people lose their destiny.
“Why am I here? I should be king.”
But instead, he said with his life:
“God placed me here. I will serve.”
Because David’s harp could soothe a king…
but it could not save him.
Temporary relief is not the same as transformation.
And this is where the Gospel explodes into the story.
Because we are not just like David.
Broken in ways we don’t always admit.

“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”
— Romans 3:23
That includes every hidden thought, every quiet compromise, every secret struggle.
And this is where Jesus enters.

“Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures… He was buried… and He was raised on the third day.”
— 1 Corinthians 15:3–4
Jesus didn’t come to give you temporary peace.
He came to break the power of sin.
To reconcile you back to God.

“Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away; behold, the new has come.”
— 2 Corinthians 5:17
So here’s the moment of truth.
Are you just easing your conscience…
or are you surrendering your life?
or are you ready for redemption?
Because Jesus is not looking for part-time worshippers.
your “harp season” is not about them.
Teaching you how to carry His presence into difficult places.
So when your flesh says, “I deserve better”…
Where have you been serving… but not surrendered?
But as a doorway to grace.
Because the same God who saw David in the shadows…
And in Christ, your hidden obedience is never wasted.
